<Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez>: Employee ownership is a term for any arrangement in which employees share in the profit and losses of a company, often owning share of the stock in the company.\1\ Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs), worker cooperatives, equity compensation plans and profit-sharing plans (PSPs) are common forms of employee ownership.\2\ A central principle of all employee-owned companies is that the interests of the employees and owners are aligned. As a business expands, generating more revenue and profits, a direct connection is drawn between an employee's work and how much they are compensated, thereby creating a culture of ownership.
\1\National Center for Employee Ownership. ``What Is Employee Ownership?.'' (Last Accessed: September 23, 2025).
\2\Id.
Employee-owned companies have many other benefits, including, but not limited to, building retirement security for employees, allowing business owners to successfully transition a business to new owners, and allowing employees a voice in management decisions.\3\ As of 2022, the most recent year for which data is available, there were 6,548 ESOPs in the U.S., holding a total of over $1.8 trillion in assets.\4\ According to the National Cooperative Business Association (NCBA), 1 in 3 Americans are co-op members, and about 65,000 cooperatives operate in the U.S., generating more than $324 billion in total revenue.\5\ Employee-owned businesses are important to job growth and contribute to the resiliency of the U.S. economy.
\3\Id.
\4\NCEO. ``Employee Ownership by the Numbers.'' (Last Accessed: September 23, 2025).
\5\National Cooperative Business Association. ``2025 Cooperative Impact Report, Building a Better World Through Cooperatives.'' (2025).
Historically, the Small Business Administration (SBA) has failed to fully engage with employee-owned businesses. The SBA has provided only limited access to their products, including the Agency's flagship 7(a) program and offered little technical support to employee-owned businesses. As a result, both ESOPs and cooperatives have faced significant challenges in accessing the SBA's lending programs over the years. In fact, from Fiscal Year FY 2022 (FY 2022) through FY 2024, the SBA only approved five 7(a) loans to assist ESOPs and only 87 7(a) loans to co-ops.\6\ In FY 2025, the SBA has only approved two 7(a) loans with a cumulative value of $900,000 to ESOPs and only 12 7(a) loans to co-ops with a cumulative value of about $9.6 million.\7\
\6\U.S. Small Business Administration. 7(a) & 504 Summary Report. (Last Accessed: September 23, 2025).
\7\Id.
In the past, SBA has even acknowledged that its policies were not achieving its goal of increasing employee ownership of businesses.\8\ During the Biden Administration, the SBA began to change its lending policies to increase capital opportunities for employee-owned businesses and engage with employee-owned businesses more directly.\9\ The Improving SBA Engagement on Employee Ownership Act would build on the steps the SBA took during the Biden Administration and improve the SBA's engagement with employee-owned businesses and cooperatives.
\8\87 Fed. Reg. 64724 (Oct. 26, 2022).
\9\Id.; White House. ``White House Convening on Worker Ownership.'' Indian Treaty Room. (Thursday, July 25, 2024).
Nydia M. Velazquez,
Ranking Member.
